turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics and training patterns

**What the training data rewards (in this n-i-p MAPbI₃ set):**

1. **SnO₂-based or SnO₂-modified compact ETLs** deliver the top results: the best training device (20.85%) is **TiO₂-c | SnO₂-np** with Spiro-MeOTAD; SnO₂-np + PTAA gives 18.19%; SnO₂-c | PCBM-60 + Spiro gives 17.28–18.0%. SnO₂ offers deeper conduction band (better electron extraction, less back-transfer), high mobility, and low UV photocatalytic degradation vs bare TiO₂.
2. **Fullerene interlayers on oxide ETLs** (TiO₂-c | PCBM-60 or C60) passivate oxide traps and reduce interface recombination — TiO₂-c | PCBM-60 with PCDTBT1 hit 19.35%; TiO₂-c | C60 + PTAA gave 16.5%.
3. **Well-doped, selective HTLs** (Spiro-MeOTAD, PTAA, doped TaTm) with **Au or MoO₃-buffered contacts** dominate the >16% region; the all-evaporated C60;PhIm | C60 / TaTm | F6-TCNNQ stack reached 17.9%.
4. Carbon electrodes, quantum-dot/exotic HTLs, HTL-free and flexible substrates cluster below ~14%.

**Matching pool candidates to these winning motifs:**

- **c064** — SLG | FTO, **TiO₂-c | SnO₂-np**, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au: near-replica of the 20.85% champion recipe (same ETL bilayer and HTL; Au contact is if anything more stable/deeper work function than Ag).
- **c005** — SLG | ITO, **TiO₂-c | PCBM-60**, PCDTBT8, MoO₃ | Au: direct analog of the 19.35% device (PCDTBT1); fullerene-passivated TiO₂ plus a hydrophobic polymer HTL with MoO₃ buffer.
- **c068** — **SnO₂-np | TiO₂-np**, PTAA, Au | MoO₃: SnO₂-np + PTAA gave 18.19%; the TiO₂-np capping improves wetting/electron selectivity, MoO₃-buffered Au is a clean ohmic hole contact.
- **c017** — **C60;PhIm | C60**, TaTm | F6-TCNNQ; TaTm, Ag, co-evaporation: matches the 17.9% fully-evaporated stack (only Ag instead of Au); doped organic transport layers give excellent selectivity and conformal films.
- **c073** — **TiO₂-c | C60**, PTAA, Ag: exact match to the 16.5% training entry, with an HMDS-scaffold ITO that mainly adds light management; fullerene-passivated interface + PTAA is a proven >16% combination.

Runner-ups considered: c083 (biguanide-passivated TiO₂, cf. 17.37% acid-passivated analog), c031, c035 — all good but slightly below the direct analogs above.

Final: c064, c005, c068, c017, c073
